benchmark.category: a voice-ordered fireworks stand with a public crew video wall for TikTok dance crews
benchmark.users: dance crews in Phnom Penh planning 15-second TikTok fireworks shots, uploading or posting clips, liking other crews' clips and checking the top crews of the week

requirements.source_phrase: No login or accounts.
requirements.statement: Public flows need no account: GET /api/catalog, POST /api/shot-kit, POST /api/transcribe, GET /api/trends, POST /api/orders, POST /api/clips, GET /api/clips, POST /api/clips/{id}/like and GET /api/clips/{id}/video all succeed with no credentials, while /sign-in, /api/me and every /api/admin route require a signed-in user; no screen in the build, preview, order, upload, like or wall flow asks the visitor to log in.
requirements.notes: Amended because the new admin moderation introduces accounts; the original no-account rule is preserved for every public flow, including the new upload and like routes.

requirements.statement: POST /api/shot-kit/{id}/edit and GET /api/shot-kit/{id} succeed with no credentials like the existing kit, trends, catalog and order routes, and the only routes that require a signed-in user are /api/me and the /api/admin routes; no screen in the build, edit, preview or order flow asks the user to log in.
requirements.notes: Removes the now-false 'there is still no account system' clause while keeping the public kit routes anonymous.

requirements.source_phrase: Clip Moderation: Add a simple admin review so new wall posts appear only after you approve them
requirements.statement: The home screen shows a Crew Video Wall section listing only the approved clips crews have posted, each entry rendered from GET /api/clips and reachable on the page without opening a dialog or another route; pending and rejected clips never appear in it.
requirements.notes: Amended for moderation: the wall was approved-only after the new review step, while the original wall request and position on the home page are kept.

requirements.source_phrase: Clip Moderation: Add a simple admin review so new wall posts appear only after you approve them
requirements.statement: After a preview clip finishes recording, the preview shows a post panel with a control that uploads that clip with a crew name to the crew wall for moderation; posting it returns a pending-review confirmation and does not add the clip to the public wall until an admin approves it.
requirements.notes: Reverses the inherited 'posting makes the clip appear on the wall' until approval; the post panel itself and its crew-name field remain.

requirements.source_phrase: Crew Video Wall: Show a gallery of recorded clips that crews post after their BoomDrop shoots
requirements.statement: GET /api/clips returns 200 with a JSON array of only approved, non-deleted clips, each carrying id, crew_name, posted time, week_likes and a playable video reference, sorted by week_likes descending then newest first, plus a top_crews list of crews with their week like totals highest first; pending, rejected and is_deleted clips are excluded and an empty store returns empty arrays.
requirements.notes: Combines the new approval-only public listing with likes and top-crews ordering; replaces the inherited newest-first, all-posted listing.

requirements.source_phrase: Upload Shoot Videos: Let crews upload the real video from their phone shoot straight to the Crew Video Wall
requirements.statement: POST /api/clips accepts a video body (preview recording or real shoot video) with a crew_name and an optional kit_id, stores exactly one clip with status pending, returns 200 with its id and status pending, and creates no public wall entry until approved; a non-video content type returns 400, a missing crew name returns 400, an unknown kit_id returns 404, and each refusal stores no row and no blob.
requirements.notes: Build test list says POST /api/clips returns {status: pending} and the clip does not appear in GET /api/clips until approved; real shoot videos may have no kit, so kit_id is optional.

requirements.source_phrase: Smooth Wall Playback: Make wall clips play and skip instantly on iPhone, with a clear error if a clip is broken
requirements.statement: Each wall entry plays its approved clip inline in a video element whose source returns the stored bytes with a video content type, on iPhone as well as desktop; a clip whose bytes cannot be loaded or decoded shows a readable error tile in the selected language with its crew name, while the other clips stay playable.
requirements.notes: Amended for the iPhone inline-playback and per-tile broken-clip error promises; the inherited fallback rule now names the error text rather than only a blank-box fallback.

requirements.source_phrase: Wall Likes: Let visitors like clips and show the top crews of the week first on the wall
requirements.statement: Each wall entry shows the crew name, the name of the kit the clip was recorded from when it has one, when it was posted and its current week like count, all read from the stored clip row rather than invented on the client.
requirements.notes: Amended so the wall identifies the crew a viewer can rank or like; real shoot uploads without a kit still show a crew name.

requirements.source_phrase: Clip Moderation: Add a simple admin review so new wall posts appear only after you approve them
requirements.statement: Posting a finished clip closes the post panel, adds the clip to the reviewer queue with a pending-review confirmation in the same session, and does not add it to the public wall or remove the wall's empty message until an admin approves it; after approval a reload lists it.
requirements.notes: Replaces the inherited immediate wall insertion with the approval gate; the user is told the post is pending rather than left to think it was lost.

requirements.statement: The post/upload control is disabled while an upload is in flight and a double press or repeated click posts exactly one pending clip, so the review queue gains one row and the public wall gains none until approval.
requirements.notes: Keeps the inherited one-upload rule while accounting for moderation: one row in the queue, not one entry on the wall.

requirements.statement: GET /api/clips/{id}/video serves an approved clip's stored bytes with content-type video/mp4, a non-zero Content-Length and an Accept-Ranges: bytes header; an unknown id, a pending clip or a rejected clip returns 404 without returning any clip data.
requirements.notes: Build test list requires content-type video/mp4; approval-only privacy means pending and rejected ids must not serve bytes.

requirements.source_phrase: Clip Moderation: Add a simple admin review so new wall posts appear only after you approve them
requirements.statement: After a clip is approved and posted, reloading / and opening the app in a new browser session both still list that clip on the Crew Video Wall with the same crew name, kit label, like count and posted time.
requirements.notes: Persistence now begins at approval, not at posting; a pending clip surviving a reload is not yet a public wall entry.

requirements.statement: GET /api/clips, POST /api/clips, GET /api/clips/{id}/video and POST /api/clips/{id}/like all succeed with no credentials, while GET /api/admin/clips and the approve/reject routes require a signed-in allowed admin; no clip response carries a provider key, token, storage path or server filesystem detail.
requirements.notes: Updates the inherited no-account rule for the public clip routes while adding the new admin auth boundary; the public upload remains anonymous.

requirements.source_phrase: Upload Shoot Videos: Let crews upload the real video from their phone shoot straight to the Crew Video Wall
requirements.statement: Every stored clip carries the crew_name it was posted with and, when it came from a preview, the kit_id it was recorded from; the wall's kit label resolves to that kit's stored name when the kit exists, and a clip without a readable kit still lists with its crew name and does not fail GET /api/clips.
requirements.notes: Real shoot uploads may have no kit, so the kit reference is optional while crew_name is always stored; a dangling kit reference must degrade, not crash the wall.

requirements.statement: POST /api/clips refuses an empty body, a missing crew_name, an oversized video over the configured limit and a non-video content type with a 4xx whose body says which limit was broken, without reading the whole oversized file and without leaving a clip row or stored blob behind.
requirements.notes: Adds the crew-name boundary to the inherited upload limits; the user's real shoot uploads can be large, so the size refusal must not read the entire stream.

requirements.source_phrase: Smooth Wall Playback: Make wall clips play and skip instantly on iPhone, with a clear error if a clip is broken
requirements.statement: GET /api/clips/{id}/video answers a Range request with 206 and the requested byte slice with a Content-Range header, advertises Accept-Ranges: bytes, and without Range returns 200 with the full video and Accept-Ranges: bytes, all with content-type video/mp4, so a browser video element can start and seek a posted clip instantly on iPhone.
requirements.notes: Build test list gives the exact 206/Content-Range and 200/Accept-Ranges cases and content-type video/mp4; this is the backend half of 'play and skip instantly'.

requirements.source_phrase: Wall Likes: Let visitors like clips and show the top crews of the week first on the wall
requirements.statement: The Crew Video Wall lists approved clips belonging to the crews with the most likes in the current week first, within that ordering newest posted first, and shows each entry's relative posted time, so a crew checking after their shoot sees the top crews at the top and the latest post first within a crew.
requirements.notes: Reverses the inherited newest-first wall ordering for top crews of the week; newest-first remains the tie-breaker within a crew.

requirements.statement: A signed-out visitor can still build a kit, open the preview, order, upload a clip, like a clip and see the wall; only /admin and the admin endpoints require sign-in, so a visitor is never sent to /sign-in from the home flow.
requirements.notes: Product shell: the new admin sign-in must not spread to the public wall, upload, like, build or order flows; keeps the inherited no-account rule for those routes.

requirements.source_phrase: Email and Password Login; Emergent-managed Google Sign-In
requirements.statement: Opening /sign-in signed out renders an email field, a password field and a submit control, and signing in with admin+clerk_test@boomdrop.dev and Boomdrop-test-123! lands the user signed in and able to reach /admin, while a wrong password shows a readable error and grants no session.
requirements.notes: User's answer to the sign-in question; Clerk bot protection blocks headless password sign-in, so tests should use a sign-in ticket from /app/memory/test_credentials.md. The page is the only new entry point.

requirements.source_phrase: Email and Password Login; Emergent-managed Google Sign-In
requirements.statement: The /sign-in screen offers an Emergent-managed Google sign-in control that starts the OAuth flow and returns to / signed in with the Google account's email and role, and a provider refusal returns to /sign-in with a readable error and no session.
requirements.notes: The user chose Emergent-managed Google Sign-In; test the registered callback and state check, and that refusal is visible rather than a blank page.

requirements.statement: A signed-in user can sign out from the app, after which /admin redirects to /sign-in and any request to an admin endpoint with the old session is refused.
requirements.notes: Product shell implied by the sign-in answer: a session needs an exit, and a signed-out screen must make no further signed-in requests.

requirements.statement: Opening /admin while signed out redirects to /sign-in and renders no pending clip, review control or admin data.
requirements.notes: Build test list requires signed-out /admin to redirect to /sign-in rather than render blank or leak the queue.

requirements.statement: Opening /admin signed in as member+clerk_test@boomdrop.dev shows an explicit no-access message and renders no pending clips or approve/reject controls.
requirements.notes: Build test list names admin-no-access for a member; the denied screen must not mount the review queue.

requirements.source_phrase: Clip Moderation: Add a simple admin review so new wall posts appear only after you approve them
requirements.statement: Opening /admin signed in as an allowed admin lists every pending clip in a review queue with its crew name, a video preview and approve and reject controls, and approving or rejecting removes it from the queue.
requirements.notes: Build test list names admin-review-queue and approve/reject; one queue covers preview recordings and real shoot uploads.

requirements.statement: The page footer shows an admin link that navigates to /admin when activated, and the link is reachable at 390px and 1280px wide.
requirements.notes: Build test list names footer-admin-link going to /admin; the route guard still decides whether the queue renders.

requirements.source_phrase: Upload Shoot Videos: Let crews upload the real video from their phone shoot straight to the Crew Video Wall
requirements.statement: The home page shows an upload control for a real shoot video from the phone's library or camera; choosing a video uploads it, shows progress, and on success shows a pending-review confirmation with no clip yet added to the public Crew Video Wall.
requirements.notes: Build summary says only preview recordings could be posted before; this adds real shoot uploads and puts them behind the new approval step.

requirements.source_phrase: Clip Moderation: Add a simple admin review so new wall posts appear only after you approve them
requirements.statement: A clip in pending or rejected status never appears on the home Crew Video Wall or in its count, while an approved clip does appear after the wall reloads.
requirements.notes: Frontend half of approval-only public wall; pending and rejected must be visibly absent, not shown dimmed.

requirements.source_phrase: Smooth Wall Playback: Make wall clips play and skip instantly on iPhone, with a clear error if a clip is broken
requirements.statement: On a 390x844 iPhone viewport an approved wall clip plays inline in its tile without taking over the screen, starts playing within a few seconds of the tap, and the user can pause and seek forward to a later second.
requirements.notes: Build open item says wall videos were sent in one piece so iPhone may not play them or allow skipping ahead; the fix requires playsinline playback backed by byte ranges.

requirements.source_phrase: Smooth Wall Playback: Make wall clips play and skip instantly on iPhone, with a clear error if a clip is broken
requirements.statement: A wall clip whose video fails to load or decode shows a readable error in the selected language on its own tile, while the other clips on the wall stay playable and the page does not crash.
requirements.notes: Build open item says a broken clip currently shows no error; the error must be per tile and not turn the whole wall into a failure state.

requirements.source_phrase: Wall Likes: Let visitors like clips and show the top crews of the week first on the wall
requirements.statement: Each approved clip on the Crew Video Wall shows a like control with its current like count; tapping it once increments the displayed count by one and shows the button in its filled/liked state, a second tap on the same device leaves the count unchanged, and the count is the same after a reload.
requirements.notes: Build test list requires the like button to fill and increment; the count must be read from the API response, not computed only in the browser.

requirements.source_phrase: Wall Likes: Let visitors like clips and show the top crews of the week first on the wall
requirements.statement: The home Crew Video Wall orders approved clips so clips belonging to the crews with the most likes this week come first, shows each clip's crew name and week like count, and breaks ties by newest posted first.
requirements.notes: Build test list says clips are sorted by week_likes descending and top_crews lists crews with likes; ordering must visibly put the top crews first.

requirements.statement: Before the real shoot video is accepted the upload panel requires a crew name, and submitting with no crew name shows a validation message and sends no upload.
requirements.notes: Build summary says wall clips are posted with a crew name; the panel must collect it, and the server must refuse a missing one.

requirements.statement: Choosing a non-video file, an empty file or a file over the size limit shows a readable error in the selected language, leaves the upload control usable, and stores no clip.
requirements.notes: Failure path of the new upload; build test list requires a non-video POST to return 400 and leave the wall unchanged.

requirements.statement: When no clips are pending, /admin shows an explicit no-clips-to-review message and no approve/reject controls rather than a blank queue or a permanent spinner.
requirements.notes: Zero-row state of the review queue; after approving every pending clip the admin must see a resolved empty state.

requirements.statement: At 390x844 and at 1280x800 /admin renders the review queue and its approve/reject controls without horizontal overflow, clipped controls or overlap, and each pending clip has an identifiable crew name and video preview.
requirements.notes: Layout class for the new admin surface at the product's two test widths.

requirements.statement: After the wall, upload, likes and moderation changes, building a kit from a typed request, opening the 3D preview, ordering and reaching the confirmation still works at 390x844 and no wall or admin control blocks the mic, text box, kit card or order dialog.
requirements.notes: Build test list regression smoke on 390x844; the new home blocks must not displace or cover the core flow.

requirements.statement: admin+clerk_test@boomdrop.dev and member+clerk_test@boomdrop.dev both sign in with the password Boomdrop-test-123!, the admin account holds the admin role and the member account holds the member role.
requirements.notes: Required credentials give these exact accounts and password; later phases sign in with them and use a Clerk sign-in ticket where bot protection blocks headless password sign-in.

requirements.statement: The wall contains one seeded approved clip with id 142b04a0-87f3-4a1d-8f80-4f4166db7502, crew name 'Clip QA Crew', status approved and exactly 1 like.
requirements.notes: The agent context note supplies this exact seeded clip and like count; it is the fixture for wall listing, likes and top-crews checks.

requirements.source_phrase: Email and Password Login; Emergent-managed Google Sign-In
requirements.statement: The backend signs a user in through Clerk using email/password and the Emergent-managed Google flow, returns a session token to the client, validates that token on /api/me and every admin route, and keeps CLERK_SECRET_KEY server-side only.
requirements.notes: Third-party integration class: word it as a real request through Clerk with the configured secret; the Google callback must check its state and map the provider's refusal to a visible error.

requirements.statement: After sign-out or Clerk session revocation, the old token is refused by /api/me and every admin endpoint with 401 and returns no user or clip data.
requirements.notes: A session that keeps working after sign-out would let a shared phone keep admin access.

requirements.statement: No Clerk secret key, Google client secret, provider token or session secret appears in any API response body, page source, JS bundle or server log line; the browser holds only the public session token.
requirements.notes: Access-control class: secrets never reach the client; search the served bundle and all API responses for the key values.

requirements.statement: GET /api/admin/clips with no token returns 401, with member+clerk_test@boomdrop.dev's token returns 403 and no list, and with an allowed admin token returns 200; the same server-side check refuses a member's direct approve/reject request, and a role field in a request body is ignored except through the admin role endpoint.
requirements.notes: Build test list gives the exact 401/403/200 cases and the ignored body role; the check must live on the server, not only in the screen.

requirements.source_phrase: yahoo or gmail
requirements.statement: The set of accounts allowed to approve clips is email addresses at yahoo.com or gmail.com; any signed-in account at another domain receives 403 from the approve/reject endpoints and sees no review queue.
requirements.notes: The user answered the admin allowlist question with 'yahoo or gmail'; this records it as domains yahoo.com and gmail.com as an assumption. The build's test credentials use admin+clerk_test@boomdrop.dev, so Phase 4 should report whether the seeded operator admin is exempted or refused by this rule.

requirements.statement: PATCH /api/admin/users/{id}/role changes a user's role only for an allowed admin; demoting the only remaining admin returns 409 and changes nothing; promoting a member or demoting an admin takes effect on that user's next request; a role field in a sign-up or profile body is ignored.
requirements.notes: Build test list names PATCH demoting the only admin -> 409 and a body role ignored except via the admin endpoint.

requirements.statement: GET /api/admin/clips for an allowed admin returns exactly the pending clips with id, crew name, posted time and a video URL, an empty queue returns an empty array, and POST /api/admin/clips/{id}/approve and /reject move a pending clip to approved or rejected exactly once, return the updated clip, change nothing on a second decision and return 404 for an unknown id.
requirements.notes: Build test list names the admin list, approve and reject flows and requires pending -> approved/rejected without a second transition.

requirements.statement: GET /api/clips/{id}/video for a pending or rejected clip returns 404 to an anonymous or member caller and returns the bytes only to an allowed admin, so an unapproved clip cannot be played by a guessed id from outside.
requirements.notes: Paranoid privacy half of approval-only moderation: hiding a pending clip from the wall is not enough if its video route still serves it.

requirements.statement: After approval GET /api/clips lists the clip on every request and after a server restart, and after rejection no GET /api/clips or GET /api/clips/{id}/video returns it.
requirements.notes: Data/persistence class: approval and rejection must be stored statuses, not transient in-memory flags; the agent note asks test clips to be soft-deleted afterward.

requirements.statement: POST /api/clips/{id}/like with a device_id increments the clip's week_likes by 1 only for the first like from that device for that clip in the current week, leaves it unchanged on a repeat from the same device, increments it for a different device_id, returns the updated count, returns 400 for a missing device_id and 404 for an unknown, pending or rejected clip.
requirements.notes: Build test list requires a same-device second like to count once and a different device to add one; the count must be the stored value.

requirements.statement: GET /api/clips returns only approved, non-deleted clips, each with crew_name, posted time and week_likes, sorted by week_likes descending and then newest first; it also returns a top_crews list of crew names with their week like totals, highest first, and an empty store returns empty arrays.
requirements.notes: Build test list names week_likes sorting and top_crews; this replaces the inherited newest-first ordering for public listing.

requirements.statement: week_likes for a clip counts only likes whose created time is within the current rolling seven-day window, so a like from eight days ago no longer counts and top_crews ranks by that same window.
requirements.notes: Assumption recorded: 'of the week' is implemented as a rolling last-seven-days window ending now; if the app uses a calendar week, the same boundary rule must apply to both week_likes and top_crews.
